newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar weakens on soft employment data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar weakens on soft employment data.

text.p: FORECAST RANGE 1.3880/1.3940 ASIAN CLOSE 1.3878
RESISTANCE 1.3795 SUPPORT 1.3945 HI 1.3895 LO 1.3864
CANADA OPEN 1.3892/97 HI 1.3895 EUROPE OPEN 1.3876

* Canada's dollar opened weaker at C$1.3892 (US$0.7198) on Friday after the release of unexpectedly soft employment data, traders said. * They said a Statistics Canada report showing a loss of 79,000 full-time jobs in July and a modest gain of only 15,000 jobs overall in the month gave investors a reason to sell the Canada dollar.
The Canadian dollar opened weaker at C$1.3892 (US$0.7198) in steady trading on Friday after the release of unexpectedly soft Canadian employment data for July, traders said.
They said a Statistics Canada report showing a loss of 79,000 full-time jobs and a modest gain of only 15,000 jobs overall in the month gave investors a reason to sell the Canada dollar.
Statistics Canada also reported that Canada's unemployment rate dipped to 9.0 percent in July, down a touch from 9.1 percent in June.

A Reuters forecast of economists predicted employment would grow by 35,500 in July after an increase of 52,000 in June. The same forecast said Canada's unemployment rate would remain unchanged at 9.1 percent.
"People are clearly disappointed. They liked the 9.0 percent but not the other background numbers," said a trader with a Canadian bank.
"Now that these numbers are out, people are pretty bearish on the Canada (dollar)," the trader said. "We are very vulnerable to a weakening off to C$1.3940 (US$0.7173) or C$1.3950 (US$0.7168) today."
Analysts said a sudden weakening of the Canadian dollar might dispell some traders' speculation of an immediate Bank of Canada interest rate hike.

"I think the market is going to say that, given the drop in full-time employment, the Bank of Canada wouldn't dare raise rates," said Andrew Pyle, vice-president of fixed income research with ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett.
But Pyle said the bank could surprise markets again, as it did with its last interest rate hike on June 26, if the Canadian dollar weakens off beyond the key C$1.3940 (US$0.7173) level.
Pyle said that strong job numbers in June might help to overshadow the weaker July data and keep the Bank of Canada in rate hike mode.
"I take the opposite view on the job data. I think if you take the two months June and July together on the employment side, the bank actually will see strength here," Pyle said.
"Things aren't as weak as this report (for July) portrays," Pyle added.
But even another rate hike may not be enough to initiate a strong rebound in the currency. "The most you're going to get is a bounce back to C$1.3800 (US$0.7246)," Pyle predicted.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar fell to 84.05 Japanese yen from 85.23 on Thursday and dipped to 1.3330 marks from Thursday's 1.3452 marks.
((Paul Simao, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8104))
